decisions.evidence: Pending-human. The question about the opening cantillation and the Divine Name holam in Mi Khamokha (116) has already gone to the human, so I am not settling it. What the pixels show (s116 band1, mi116.png, full page): the line is printed with cantillation throughout, so OURS is wrong to leave it all out. There are visible marks under כמכה (a '>'-shaped stroke), under/over בָּאֵלִם, a cluster of dots above יהוה, and marks under מי, כמכה, נאדר, the etnach under בקדש, and marks under נורא, עשה and פלא. Whether THEIRS has the exact accent names and host letters right, including the holam over the ה of the Name, is the open human question.

s116 band2, line 3 (between טוֹבִים and הַכֹּל), checked on the full page: the word has only four letters, ו־ק־נ־ה. There is no vav between ק and נ, and a holam dot sits over the ק. This is a defective spelling and is kept literally. Compare plene וְזוֹכֵר on the same line, which does have a vav.

s116 band2, line 3, the last word at the left margin. The patah under ח, the shva under ס and the tsere under ד are visible. I can't confidently confirm or rule out a dagesh dot inside the ד at band or full-page resolution: there is a dark speck near the top of the ד's bowl, but I can't tell it apart from the letter's own stroke or ink spread. The grammatically expected dagesh can't be filled in from memory. A tight high-resolution crop of this one word is needed.

s116 band3, last line, and the full page: there is a plain space between בְּכָל and יוֹם with no raised maqaf stroke. On the same page the maqafs in מִי־כָמֹכָה and עַל־שְׂפַת are clearly visible as raised bars, so a maqaf would have shown here if it were printed.
s117 band2, 'for their children’s children': the apostrophe is the typeface's curly, comma-shaped right single quote (’), not a straight vertical tick. The straight ' in THEIRS is a normalization.
s117 band2, 'for His Name’s sake in love': the same curly typographic apostrophe (’). The straight ' in THEIRS is a normalization.
